question.leadin: Democrat Pat Schroeder described this man's presidency as "Teflon-coated" because "nothing sticks to him."
question.text: Name this president who somehow survived scandals like the Iran-Contra Affair during his two terms in office in the 1980s.
question.clue: His Secretary of State, Alexander Haig, stated "I am in control here" after John Hinckley attempted to assassinate this president.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about mink in history.
swap.text: This president claimed that his wife, Pat, "doesn't have a mink coat" in his "Checkers" speech. This man was later forced to resign over the Watergate scandal, despite declaring "I am not a crook".
swap.clue: A ruling in which this man was the respondent cited Accardi v. Shaughnessy to assert the power of the Attorney General and notes that "in camera inspection" is not a substantial diminishment of communications.

question.text: Reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein of the Washington Post used this anonymous source during their reporting on the scandal. In 2005, former FBI Associate Director Mark Felt stepped forward as the source.
question.clue: The only person explicitly ruled out by those who know for sure is Alexander Haig.

swap.text: This commander of the Apollo 11 mission, the first man to set foot on the moon, passed away in August 2012.
swap.clue: JFK's wish for a man on the moon was fulfilled when this astronaut made "one giant leap for mankind," becoming the first American on the moon.

question.leadin: According to notes by H.R. Haldeman, this diplomat helped the Nixon campaign sabotage the Johnson administration's peace talks in Vietnam.
question.text: Name this Secretary of State who, along with Le Duc Tho (LAY duk TAO), won the Nobel Prize for negotiating the Paris Peace Accords.
question.clue: This man, who may have coordinated the assassination of Archbishop Makarios, coined the term "constructive ambiguity" to describe his policy toward China.

swap.leadin: Name these politicians and people associated with politics.
swap.text: This Democratic lawmaker from Texas served as speaker for seventeen years, the longest tenure in history. Name this man who served under Eisenhower, Kennedy, Truman, and Roosevelt.
swap.clue: Known as "Mr. Democrat", this man was elected to the House in 1912 and served forty-eight years in that body, including a record seventeen years as House speaker.

question.leadin: This man served as both President of Columbia University and President of the United States.
question.text: Name this man who was the Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces in Europe during World War II and whose vice president was Richard Nixon. He was succeeded by John F. Kennedy.
question.clue: Both Operation PBSUCCESS, which kicked Jacobo Arbenz out of office, and Operation Ajax were overseen by this president's administration.

swap.text: One notable Minnesotan politician was this Carter vice president and opponent of Ronald Reagan in the 1984 presidential election.
swap.clue: In 1984, Ronald Reagan won re-election over this Democrat-Jimmy Carter's former vice-president-by winning every state except this man's home state, Minnesota.

question.leadin: The four principles of "Americanism" were asserted in Margaret Chase Smith's "Declaration of Conscience" speech attacking this man.
question.text: Name this target of an attack by Joseph Welch.
question.clue: This man's actions with Owen Lattimore involved the creation of the Tydings Committee.

swap.leadin: This event was sparked by thousands of people who rushed the Peruvian embassy trying to seek asylum.
swap.text: Name this 1980 event in which large numbers of people, many of them released prisoners, boarded ramshackle crafts headed to Florida from the namesake town.
swap.answerHtml: Mariel Boatlift [prompt on but DO NOT REVEAL Cuban Boatlift]
swap.clue: Some participants in this event staged a riot at Fort Chaffee, Arkansas, which briefly derailed the career of Governor Bill Clinton.

question.text: In the 1970s, the CIA's misdeeds were investigated by a committee led by and named for this Democratic senator from Idaho, which led to the passage of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, or FISA ("FYE-zuh").
question.answerHtml: Frank Church [or Frank Forrester Church III; accept Church Committee]
question.clue: The Lockheed bribery scandals were exposed by this senator, who helped to create his state's River of No Return Wilderness Area, which now bears his name.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about "dirty tricks" employed by the Nixon campaign during the 1972 presidential election.
swap.text: During the Democratic primaries, Nixon operatives forged the so-called "Canuck Letter," which alleged that this Maine senator and former running mate of Hubert Humphrey was prejudiced against French Canadians.
swap.clue: He later became Secretary of State after the resignation of Cyrus Vance under Jimmy Carter.

question.text: The Dodd-Frank Reform Act contained a rule named for this chairman of the Federal Reserve who was succeeded by Alan Greenspan.
question.clue: This Fed chairman under Carter and Reagan was credited with combatting the high inflation of the 1970s and 1980s. This man's namesake "rule" seeks to discourage banks from making certain types of speculative investments.

swap.leadin: Name some things about the nefarious presence of Iver Johnson guns in US History.
swap.text: This Palestinian assassin used an Iver Johnson gun to kill Robert Kennedy during the 1968 Democratic Primaries.
swap.clue: This Palestinian national shot and killed RFK in 1968 because Kennedy had supported Israel during the Six-Day War.

question.text: This scandal of the Reagan administration involved the sale of arms to one country to provide funds to support anti-Sandanista rebels in Nicaragua.
question.clue: Admiral John Poindexter was convicted of obstruction of justice and Fawn Hall became the most famous secretary in the United States when she admitted to shredding documents for her boss during the hearings over this.

swap.text: This historian ended up on the enemies list after he attacked Nixon in The Imperial Presidency. This former special assistant to JFK glorified the Kennedy presidency in his book A Thousand Days.
swap.answerHtml: Arthur Schlesinger Jr. [do not accept or prompt on “Arthur Schlesinger Sr.”]
swap.clue: This Pulitzer-prize winning historian of The Imperial Presidency detailed the controversy of JFK needing voter support from McCarthy supporters in his book A Thousand Days.

question.text: In this 1951 decision, the Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of the Smith Act, which was determined not to violate the First Amendment

swap.leadin: Name these ships which caused some crazy affairs in American history.
swap.text: This intelligence ship commanded by Lloyd Bucher was captured by North Korea in 1968, sparking a crisis that was reinvigorated when Korean leaders discovered that Bucher's supposed confession implied that he'd like to pee on Kim il Sung.
swap.clue: The agreement ending this affair permitted the U.S. to disavow the confessions of the crewmen to intruding into foreign waters.

question.text: Under the leadership of saleswoman Brownie Wise, this line of products was widely sold in the 1950s through a form of direct marketing called the "party plan," which involved women hosting social events for their friends and neighbors to try this line of products.

swap.leadin: This man assisted Rudolf Peierls on the "Tube Alloys" project, and he provided information that led to the arrest of Harry Gold.
swap.text: Name this British citizen and theoretical physicist for the Manhattan Project. Information this man gave the Soviet Union accelerated the Soviet nuclear program by a year.
swap.clue: This man was known as an excellent babysitter to his fellow scientists but ran afoul of the Venona project while serving as the head of a division at the Harwell Research Establishment.
